issue: After Kisor v. Wilkie, should courts defer to the Sentencing Guidelines commentary only when the Guidelines text is genuinely ambiguous, or should they apply the more deferential Stinson approach?
provision: U.S.S.G. § 2L1.2 cmt. n.3 (deference to Guidelines commentary under Stinson v. United States and Kisor v. Wilkie)

sides.position: After Kisor, courts should not defer to the Guidelines commentary absent genuine ambiguity in the Guidelines text.
cases: United States v. Riccardi, 989 F.3d 476 (6th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Nasir, 982 F.3d 144 (3d Cir. 2020) (en banc), vacated on other grounds, 142 S. Ct. 56 (2021)

sides.position: Kisor does not apply to the Sentencing Commission's official commentary; courts should defer to the commentary under Stinson v. United States.
cases: United States v. Moses, 23 F.4th 347 (4th Cir. 2022)

quote: This contention is the subject of a circuit split.
cite: United States v. Cordova-Lopez, 34 F.4th 442 (5th Cir. 2022)
